title: Illuminated Orbital Shaker for Microalgae Culture
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdtyi6pw

steps.title: Procure all required components
steps.instruction: Obtain the orbital shaker (e.g., purchased on eBay), electronics parts (e.g., from Farnell), clear acrylic sheet (from a sheet‑plastic supplier or laser‑cut service), custom PCB (ordered from Seeed Technology), and a case (3‑D printed on a Stratasys Uprint SE Plus). The components can be sourced from four supplier categories: laboratory equipment suppliers, electronics parts distributors, PCB manufacturers, and 3‑D‑printing services.

steps.title: Assemble LED controller PCB
steps.instruction: Solder the surface‑mount components (including 0603‑package parts) onto the custom PCB using a soldering station, flux, and tweezers; the soldering should take 1–2 hours. After soldering, test the circuit, then clean any excess flux. Observe fire‑safety, use a fume extractor, and wear gloves.

steps.title: Print case for controller
steps.instruction: Print the LED‑controller housing on a fused‑deposition‑modeling printer (e.g., Stratasys Uprint SE Plus). The printed case may have a rough finish; a laser‑sintering printer can be used for higher detail if desired.

steps.title: Assemble cooled LED illuminator
steps.instruction: Glue LED strips to the underside of the heatsink, then solder the strips together in a daisy‑chain to connect to the LED controller. Glue the cooling fans to the heatsink and wire them to the controller as well.

steps.title: Prepare acrylic platform
steps.instruction: Cut the clear acrylic sheet to the required dimensions and drill mounting holes using a hacksaw and drill, or alternatively cut and drill with a laser cutter.

steps.title: Assemble illuminated orbital shaker
steps.instruction: Mount the acrylic sheet on the orbital shaker using metal stand‑offs, place the cooled LED illuminator beneath the acrylic, and lay the anti‑slip silicone mat on top of the acrylic. Connect the LED controller to a power socket through a 24‑hour timer programmed with the desired day/night cycle, then power on the system.
